title: O Saints, Make This Your Work
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 290
summary: This shabad opens with o friends, O Saints, make this your work. It turns the heart toward o Nanak, chant the Naam, the treasure of excellence.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels searching, hungry, and unsettled because the shabad keeps seeking inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: O Nanak, chant the Naam, the treasure of excellence.

lines.translation: O friends, O Saints, make this your work.
Renounce everything else, and chant the Name of the Lord.
Meditate, meditate, meditate in remembrance of Him, and find peace.
Chant the Naam yourself, and inspire others to chant it.
By loving devotional worship, you shall cross over the world-ocean.
Without devotional meditation, the body will be just ashes.
All joys and comforts are in the treasure of the Naam.
Even the drowning can reach the place of rest and safety.
O Nanak, chant the Naam, the treasure of excellence. ||5||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: o friends, O Saints, make this your work.
The middle movement widens the correction through without devotional meditation, the body will be just ashes.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: o Nanak, chant the Naam, the treasure of excellence.
